findings.summary: Resolve compiled backend selection in one PAL helper and report Android backend identity from the native entrypoint instead of duplicating it in Gradle and Java.
Reuse the canonical NativeBackend inventory and types while retaining strict Android token validation.
Use named Android capture options and the shared measured-run environment policy.
Reuse the shared scope guard for Dawn capability cleanup and Android window-property unlocking.
Initialize acquired surface textures in the shared acquisition helper; offscreen images retain their separate initialization.
Compile the sweep's Vulkan shaders in one invocation of the existing multi-directory compiler.
Refresh sweep input stamps once before fan-out and prevent prepared workers from regenerating them.
Fingerprint Dawn's own build inputs rather than unrelated Android packaging and smoke orchestration.
Verify Android backend and exit markers in one constant-memory pass over logcat.
Pass canonical backend names directly to the shared parity-threshold resolver.
Reuse the shared acquisition body in existing extracted-native fixtures and cover transient surface skips separately from GPU failures.
